1:
Eradicating countless epidemics, securing
safe shelter, preserving food...
2: Mankind has even ventured into space.
4:
And now, here before us, a new hardship
has arisen!
5:
The phenomenon of clothes gaining a will
of their own and flying away!!
7:
This phenomenon has persisted far longer
than anticipated!
8:
Mankind must uncover the true nature of
this hardship!!
10:
Does that have something to do with why
you dragged me here?
12:
I intend to have you assist me in
investigating the effect of the Card that
makes clothes fly away.
14:
But I haven't heard any of the details, you
know?
15:
Rest assured, I am not counting on your
knowledge.
16: I will now have you put on clothes.
17:
Is it truly impossible to wear clothes? And
if so, where exactly does "clothing"
begin?
19: First, try putting on this leaf!
20: Ahh... So that's what this is about...
21: Well, whatever. Here goes, and... slap.
25:
So it did. It appears the leaf recognized
itself as clothing.
26:
In that case, tree bark is likely the same.
What about a flat stone?
31:
The effect is broader than I expected. To
think it would recognize not just leaves,
but even stones as clothing.
32:
What shall we try next...? Tomoki, have you
any ideas?
37:
How about the idea of wearing the Earth as
clothes? I dig a hole in the ground and bury
myself in it.
38: Then it'd count as clothes, wouldn't it?
39: I suppose... Let us try it.
41:
Hm, enough for one person... This should
do.
42:
If I get in this hole, I'll be wearing the
Earth!
44:
It worked, Sugata-senpai!! Nothing's flying
away!!
47:
You can't see me naked! The experiment's a
success, isn't it?!
48:
Because while you're in a hole, you can't
walk around freely.
52:
You know how there's the "human chair,"
where a person acts as a chair?
53:
You know how people make "human
letters," where they arrange themselves
into the shape of letters?
54:
So if that works, then people could become
clothes too -- human clothes! Why not?!
60: ...It feels as though I'm being hugged.
62:
I have no trouble walking... but as clothing,
it may be a bit on the heavy side.
64: However, it does not fly away.
66:
It covers the body, and it does not fly
away. Moving around isn't impossible,
either. This could be...
68: Tomokiii, I brought you lunch... wh... wha...?!
72:
Huh? N-No... This is a human clothes
experiment!!
74:
Hmm... So it has problems in practical use,
then.
75: What if we drew them on the body?
77:
You paint the clothes right onto bare skin.
Body paint!!
78:
Tomoki, do you truly believe that could
replace clothing?!
80:
Good, let us experiment at once. Rest
assured, I can paint as well.
81: S-Sorry. On second thought, never mind.
82:
Do not lose your nerve. Where there is no
failure, there is no success!
84: Now, I shall paint clothes on your body.
86:
Tomoki, I can't paint if you thrash around
like that.
87:
(This is no good! I can't stand the tickling
long enough for him to paint my whole
body!)
